{{Quote|Let`s see what you can do with that staff.|Obi-Wan Kenobi to Magnaguards|<ref name="rots game">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref>}}
The '''electrostaff''', also known as an '''electrostave''', was a type of electrified staff weapon.<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" /><ref name="FORCE&DESTINY" /><ref name="DATABASE" />

==Description==
{{Quote|Resistant to the energy outpourings of a lightsaber, the phrik alloy staffs were potent weapons, but like any weapon they needed to find their target&hellip;|[[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]|<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>}}
[[File:MagnaGuard_FDCR.png|thumb|left|180px|A MagnaGuard wielding an electrostaff]]
Electrostaves required two standard [[Energy cell/Legends|energy cells]] to operate,<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" /> and were lined with focusing rods along the shaft; these rods fed into an electromagnetic field generator that energized a power cycling coil.<ref name="NewFF" /> Energy was then released at either end of the staff by way of electromagnetic pulse-generating tips as intense electrical charges.<ref name="DATABASE" /> These discharges could be set to a number of different outputs by the user; a shock setting used for crowd control; a powerful [[stun]] setting that could sideline even the toughest opponents; and a full-powered setting that could easily shear a sentient in half.<ref name="FORCE&DESTINY" />

On lethal settings, even glancing hits could produce terrible burns, and a direct hit to the head, throat, or heart was instant death.<ref name="STEALTH" /> A single quick jab to the chest on stun was enough to send [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] to the ground and convulsing for several minutes, though not to unconsciousness; afterwards he would suffer from severe aftereffects such as paleness, rapid pulse, inability to focus, pounding headache, and doubled vision.<ref name="STEALTH" /> Electrostaves were powerful enough to bypass protective armor and bodysuits, and were used against [[Clone trooper/Legends|Clone Troopers]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] to great effect.<ref name="DATABASE" /> Energy discharges aside, electrostaves were more than capable of lethal blunt-force trauma, and were equally used to club and shock targets to death.<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" /><ref name="FORCE&DESTINY" />

Coming into vogue during the Clone Wars, many electrostaves were made out of [[Phrik/Legends|Phrik]] alloy, and were [[Lightsaber/Legends|Lightsaber]]-resistant as a result; combined with a length of over two meters, electrostaves made ideal weapons against [[Force-sensitive/Legends|force users]] as they allowed the wielder to strike outside of the reach of a lightsaber, and to deflect any blows that slipped inside their guard.<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" /><ref name="FORCE&DESTINY" /> Likewise, the electrostaff was incredibly versatile outside of combat; it allowed for crowd-control and subduing targets non-lethally, it could neutralize [[Ray shield/Legends|energy shielding]],<ref name="NewFF">{{FactFile2013|2|ELE 1-2|Electrostaff}}</ref><ref name="DATABASE" /> short out electronics,<ref name="STEALTH" /> and was routinely used as a [[Torture/Legends|torture]] device.<ref name="NewFF" />

==History==
[[File:Dug_electrostaff.png|thumb|right|200px|[[Dug cavalier/Legends|Dug cavaliers]] wielding electrostaves]]
Electrostaves became very common during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], being widely used by [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] to kill numerous [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and were used throughout the length of the war.<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" /><ref name="FORCE&DESTINY" /><ref name="STEALTH" /><ref name="Deception" /><ref name="STEALTH" /> These [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] electrostaffs were manufactured by [[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid Armor Workshop]],<ref name="NewFF" /> and many - though not all, due to high costs - were constructed of phrik.<ref name="NewFF" />

During the Clone Wars, the [[Dug cavalier/Legends|Dug Cavaliers]] of [[Malastare]] and the slavers of [[Zygerria]] made use of a unique variant that could fold out its end like an [[Umbrella/Legends|umbrella]] when in use, producing an electrical charge that could harm both [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and living creatures.

Around [[1 BBY/Legends|1]] and [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], [[Riot stormtrooper/Legends|riot troopers]] and [[Imperial Heavy Trooper/Legends|heavy troopers]] of the Empire were known to use these staffs. They were able to resist lightsabers using [[Cortosis/Legends|Cortosis]], as shown when they engaged [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] apprentice, as well as [[Subject 1138|his clone]]. They were encountered by them on several planets, including [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]], [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], and [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], though failed to stop the apprentice and later his clone from reaching his objectives.

{{Weapon-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:ElectroguillotineElectrostaff.png|thumb|left|200px|Two MagnaGuards prepare to execute a helpless prisoner.]]
The electrostaff was devised by [[George Lucas]] as a way of presenting a threat to the until-now unstoppable Jedi with a lightsaber.<ref name="DATABASE" /> The dancing energetic charge emitted from the staff was to suggest a built-in shield mechanism that keeps a lightsaber blade from slicing through.<ref name="DATABASE" /> When the animation of the energy changed to instead flow from the tips and not across the entire pole, it was decided instead that the pole was made of specialized materials.<ref name="DATABASE" />

In ''[[Grievous Intrigue]]'', an episode of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']], [[Grievous/Legends|General Grievous]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] engaged in a battle during which Kenobi briefly makes use of an electrostaff; however, Grievous soon destroyed the staff with his sabers by cutting off both ends of it. It is unexplained whether he hit weak points on the staff or if this was a continuity error.
